# entire-brain P1 is clean and ready — #85 is `MERGEABLE/CLEAN`, CI 15/15

`+7,463/−57` across 33 files. Every fix is mutation-verified: revert it and its test fails.

## Bugs fixed
| | |
|---|---|
| **Silent data loss** | `distill --force` deleted sync-raised cross-member conflicts it can never regenerate |
| **Unremovable orphans** | a proposal with no fact head could be neither accepted nor rejected — stuck in every member's list forever |
| **Cross-clone resurrection** | a second clone republished conflicts the team had already settled |
| **Lost settlements** | *(mine, from the prior round)* entries were pruned even when there was nothing to mirror from |

## Performance
`Sync` already computes the post-sync head, so it returns it — **removing a full network round-trip from every hosted sync**. Plus no more needless fact-store write on a no-op reject.

## Accuracy
`facts proposals apply` now mirrors into the member's own facts immediately, instead of leaving their recall contradicting the decision they just made.

## Robustness
Three fuzz targets over the wire format, **12M+ executions**, no defects — fixed-point, struct/bytes agreement, and tamper rejection. Plus two load-sensitive brief tests de-flaked (one had failed my own verification on correct code).

## Two things I'd want you to read
**I was wrong once and reverted myself.** I read `Canonicalize`'s unknown-field pass-through as a flaw and made it reject — breaking `TestVerifyBytesToleratesUnknownFields`, which exists precisely to pin that behavior. The signature already covers unknown fields, so nothing can be smuggled or stripped, and the pass-through is what lets an older verifier validate a newer producer under ADR 0001. Behavior was right; the missing piece was a comment saying why, which I added.

**A latent trap defused:** all 10 vendored `gitmeta` files cited the *proof-of-concept* repo as upstream. That PR was superseded, not merged — the real engine is in entire-api. Anyone re-vendoring would have pulled from a dead branch. Header now records the true source, the two-way drift since, and why it's inert today (verified: local-only store, no remote, no shared ref).

## Left deliberately alone, flagged not hidden
The git-intent overlay's 500ms bound means it **also stops contributing to retrieval on a loaded machine in production** — the code shows that's a deliberate latency trade, so I didn't change product behavior uninvited.

**Remaining P1 blocker is unchanged and not in brain:** #242's wire disagreement with this client — paths, settle model, and 16-vs-64-hex proposal ids.

# Why P1 isn't "fully verified" yet

**1. The wire mismatch is still open — I didn't fix it.**

| | #85 (client) | #242 (server) |
|---|---|---|
| path | `/brain/facts/proposals` | `/brain/proposals` |
| settle | `POST .../{id}/resolve` | `POST .../{id}/apply` + `/reject` |
| proposal id | `sha256(action,candidate,target,branch,proposedBy)` → **16 hex** | `sha256(branch,baseRef,contentRef)` → **64 hex** |

Merging both today gives you a P1 whose two halves cannot address the same proposal. I left this deliberately: which storage seam the queue gets is an architecture call, and #242's `ProposalStore.Apply` resolving server-side contradicts ADR-P1-E ("merge runs on the runner"). My recommendation — api moves to the client's shape — is written up on #242.

**2. The live round-trip has never been run.** #64 deferred it and it's still deferred. Everything on both sides is proven against fakes; the real wire has never carried a single request. That's precisely what would have caught the mismatch above.

- **Not fixed: the api half.** One decision away from being mechanical work.
- **Never verified: the end-to-end path.**

=== my earlier migration ===
-- +goose Up
-- brain_fact_proposals — the OPEN PROPOSAL SET: fact-set contributions that have
-- been sealed into the brain store but have NOT yet been merged into a branch's
-- durable fact-set head (brain_fact_refs, 046).
--
-- Where brain_fact_refs is the single moving HEAD per (repo_key, branch), this table
-- is the review queue in front of it: a member (or a runner) opens a proposal naming
-- the head it merged against (base_ref) and the content-addressed facts blob it
-- produced (content_ref); a member with repo push then applies it — which performs
-- the SAME compare-and-swap the direct advance path performs, so a proposal whose
-- base_ref has been overtaken loses the CAS and is reported as a precondition
-- failure rather than silently clobbering the newer head — or rejects it.
--
-- One row per (repo_key, proposal_id). proposal_id is DETERMINISTIC — a hash over
-- (branch, base_ref, content_ref) — so re-opening the byte-identical proposal is
-- idempotent (it collides on the PK and returns the existing row) rather than
-- littering the queue with duplicates of the same contribution.
--
-- repo_key is the INJECTIVE tenancy key (slug@repo_ulid, see brainbuild.RepoKeyFor),
-- the same key brain_fact_refs (046), brain_fact_advances (047), and brain_deks (044)
-- use — never the lossy bare slug, which can collapse two distinct repos with
-- different ACLs into one keyspace.
--
-- Status is a one-way street: open → applied | rejected, and a terminal row never
-- moves again. That is enforced in the STATEMENT (every transition is an
-- `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'open'`, so a losing transition affects 0 rows and is
-- reported as a conflict) plus the CHECK constraint below, not merely by convention.
--
-- search_path is set here, not inherited: on an existing DB goose runs only this
-- migration, so 001_init's `SET search_path TO repo, public` never executes in this
-- session and a bare table name would resolve against the default path.
SET search_path TO repo, public;

CREATE TABLE brain_fact_proposals (
    repo_key        TEXT NOT NULL,
    proposal_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
    branch          TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- The fact-set head the proposer merged against; '' means "merged into an empty
    -- base" (a create), exactly as in FactSetStore.Advance's oldRef.
    base_ref        TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- facts-<sha256(plaintext)> — the coordinate of the sealed proposed blob
    -- (brain/{repo_key}/facts/{content_ref}).
    content_ref     TEXT NOT NULL,
    status          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'open',
    proposed_by     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    summary         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- Free-text rejection reason; '' unless status = 'rejected'.
    reason          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    -- The head this proposal became when applied ('' / 0 until then).
    applied_ref     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    applied_version BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (repo_key, proposal_id),
    CONSTRAINT brain_fact_proposals_status_chk
        CHECK (status IN ('open', 'applied', 'rejected'))
);

-- The list endpoint reads exactly one slice: this repo's OPEN proposals, optionally
-- narrowed to a branch, oldest first. A partial index on status = 'open' keeps the
-- queue scan proportional to the open set rather than to all history.
CREATE INDEX brain_fact_proposals_open_idx
    ON brain_fact_proposals (repo_key, branch, created_at)
    WHERE status = 'open';

-- The crypto-shred-on-reject path (and the supersede-shred in brain_fact_refs's
-- advance) must ask "does any non-rejected proposal still reference this facts
-- coordinate?" before dropping its DEK — a lookup by (repo_key, content_ref) the PK
-- cannot serve.
CREATE INDEX brain_fact_proposals_content_ref_idx
    ON brain_fact_proposals (repo_key, content_ref);

-- Grant exactly what the queue needs — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE — and deliberately NO
-- DELETE: a resolved proposal is retained as the record of who contributed what and
-- what happened to it. Stating the grant explicitly (rather than leaning on 001's
-- schema default privileges) makes the "no DELETE" design visible at the table's
-- birth, matching brain_deks (044), brain_overlay_branches (045), and
-- brain_fact_refs (046).
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_fact_proposals TO repo_rw;

-- Debug-readable view matching the *_readable convention: a proposal row is refs +
-- status + attribution, no secret material (the proposed facts themselves live
-- encrypted in the object store under content_ref), so expose every column.
CREATE VIEW brain_fact_proposals_readable AS
    SELECT repo_key, proposal_id, branch, base_ref, content_ref, status, proposed_by,
           summary, reason, applied_ref, applied_version, created_at, updated_at
    FROM brain_fact_proposals;

-- +goose Down
SET search_path TO repo, public;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS brain_fact_proposals_readable;
REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_fact_proposals FROM repo_rw;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS brain_fact_proposals;

-- +goose Up
-- brain_proposal_refs — the moving HEAD of a branch's OPEN PROPOSAL SET.
--
-- The open proposal set is a single content-addressed blob (the JSON array of open
-- proposals), pointed at by one compare-and-swapped ref per (repo_key, branch) — the
-- exact shape brain_fact_refs (046) gives the fact-set head, and stored through the
-- same encrypting blob store. It is deliberately NOT a row-per-proposal queue:
--
--   ADR-P1-E puts the merge on the runner. The runner reads the fact head and the
--   open set, computes the resolution locally, and compare-and-swaps BOTH back under
--   the refs it read. A server that stored proposals as rows would have to re-derive
--   which entries survive a resolution — that is merge logic, and a second
--   implementation of it is exactly the divergence the wire contract exists to stop.
--   As a blob the server never interprets the contents: it swaps a pointer.
--
--   It also keeps proposal identity single-sourced. Ids are derived by the client
--   from the proposal's own fields; a server-side id derived from storage
--   coordinates would disagree, and no proposal could be addressed across the wire.
--
-- repo_key is the INJECTIVE tenancy key (slug@repo_ulid, see brainbuild.RepoKeyFor),
-- the same key brain_fact_refs (046), brain_fact_advances (047) and brain_deks (044)
-- use — never the lossy bare slug, which can collapse two repos with different ACLs
-- into one keyspace.
--
-- search_path is set here, not inherited: on an existing DB goose runs only this
-- migration, so 001_init's `SET search_path TO repo, public` never executes in this
-- session and a bare table name would resolve against the default path.
SET search_path TO repo, public;

CREATE TABLE brain_proposal_refs (
    repo_key    TEXT NOT NULL,
    branch      TEXT NOT NULL,
    current_ref TEXT NOT NULL,
    version     BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (repo_key, branch)
);

-- Mirrors brain_fact_refs_current_ref_idx: the shred-on-supersede path counts, after
-- moving a branch off oldRef, whether any branch still references it — a scan by
-- (repo_key, current_ref) that the PK (leading repo_key, branch) cannot serve.
CREATE INDEX brain_proposal_refs_current_ref_idx ON brain_proposal_refs (repo_key, current_ref);

-- SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and deliberately NO DELETE: a head only ever moves, it is
-- never removed. Stated explicitly rather than leaning on 001's schema defaults, so
-- the "no DELETE" design is visible at the table's birth, matching 044/045/046.
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_proposal_refs TO repo_rw;

-- Debug-readable view per the *_readable convention: a head is a content ref plus a
-- version, carrying no secret material (the proposals themselves live encrypted in
-- the object store under current_ref), so expose every column.
CREATE VIEW brain_proposal_refs_readable AS
    SELECT repo_key, branch, current_ref, version, updated_at
    FROM brain_proposal_refs;

-- +goose Down
SET search_path TO repo, public;
DROP VIEW IF EXISTS brain_proposal_refs_readable;
REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON brain_proposal_refs FROM repo_rw;
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS brain_proposal_refs;

content.text:
# The wire is reconciled — both halves of P1 now speak the same contract

## What #242 was actually broken on
Three incompatibilities at once, and **every unit test on both sides passed**, because nothing exercised the boundary:

| | brain client | api (before) |
|---|---|---|
| path | `/brain/facts/proposals` | `/brain/proposals` |
| settle | `POST .../{id}/resolve` | `apply` + `reject` |
| proposal id | 16-hex from the proposal's fields | 64-hex from storage coords |

## The api side moved, and why
`ProposalStore.Apply` was re-deriving resolutions server-side — **a second implementation of merge logic**, which is precisely the divergence ADR-P1-E ("merge runs on the runner") exists to prevent. The queue also belongs under `/brain/facts/*`, where this service already serves the head. And identity can only be derived by the side that knows the proposal's fields.

So the queue is now **one CAS'd blob per branch**, not a row per proposal. The server stores bytes and moves pointers; it never interprets an entry, so a newer client can add fields with no server change. It reuses the fact-set machinery over its own ref index and blob kind.

## Two subtle things worth your eye
**`KindProposals` isn't cosmetic.** Sharing `KindFacts` would let the fact-head crypto-shred **delete a live proposal blob's DEK**, because no fact head references a proposal coordinate.

**`resolve` swaps facts first, deliberately.** Losing the set CAS after advancing facts leaves the entry queued and the runner re-resolves idempotently. The reverse order could drop the entry while facts never moved — losing the settlement outright.

## Guarding the boundary
Added a **wire-contract test fed the client's literal JSON**. The repos can't import each other, so nothing else makes a rename fail a build — which is exactly how three incompatibilities survived. And cross-checking turned up one more real bug: api answers **503** when the brain is disabled, but the client only treated 404/501 as "no queue", so it failed a sync whose facts had already landed. Fixed client-side (`c0ae25e6`).

## Where this leaves P1
- **#85** — MERGEABLE, CI re-running on the new commit
- **#242** — MERGEABLE/BLOCKED (needs approval), `+10,333/−2`, all brain tests green including the OpenAPI invariant

**One honest gap remains, and I won't paper over it:** they agree *on paper*, and the contract test pins the shapes — but the **live cross-repo round-trip has still never been run.** That's what would have caught all four of these bugs, and it needs both services actually running. Until then P1 is "reconciled and verified by contract", not "verified end to end".

func lastJSONObject(out string) string {
	start := strings.Index(out, "{")
	end := strings.LastIndex(out, "}")
	if start < 0 || end < start {

	return out[start : end+1]

# ✅ The live cross-repo round-trip **passes** — P1 is verified end to end

The real `entire-brain` binary drove the real api router over real HTTP:

```
GET /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/facts             200
GET /api/v1/repos/{repo_id}/brain/facts/proposals   200   ← the reconciled endpoint
--- PASS: TestBrainRoundTripAgainstRealClient
```

It proves the full path: real client → real URLs → real auth headers → real handlers → real CAS, **and a real data round-trip** — the server stores a proposal, the client reads it back and reports the same client-derived id. That's exactly the direction the 16-vs-64-hex divergence broke.

## What running it actually found
This is why "verified by contract" wasn't enough — the moment it ran, it found two things unit tests couldn't:

1. **A 500 panic on the allow path.** `checkRepoPermission` dereferenced a nil `Store`. The `repoExister` interface exists with the comment *"so checkRepoAccess is testable without Postgres"* — but `RepoActivityDeps.Store` is **concrete**, so the allow path was only reachable with a live database. Every in-process authz test in the repo asserts *denials* only, which short-circuit before the store. The first test to exercise an allow path panicked. Added the narrow seam that comment already implied.

2. **My own JSON extractor was wrong** — the CLI pretty-prints across lines, so a single-line matcher silently returned `{}` and the assertion read `<nil>` instead of failing loudly.

## Where P1 stands now

| | |
|---|---|
| **#85** entire-brain | client half, MERGEABLE, all fixes + fuzz coverage |
| **#242** entire-api | server half reconciled to the client's contract, MERGEABLE/BLOCKED (needs approval) |
| **wire** | paths, verbs, ids, status codes — agree, and **pinned** by a contract test fed the client's literal JSON |
| **end-to-end** | **verified live**, no longer deferred |

The round-trip is opt-in (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_BIN=...`) so it can't break normal CI, and it's documented with the exact command to run it.

What it is. The differentiator. P1 lifts the brain off the laptop into a shared, server-side, multi-tenant service, so one member's agent learns something and every other member's agent can read it. The gate is the P0 schema-freeze plus a namespace, and it deliberately relaxes the local-only guardrail. All four parts are built and DB-tested on clone branches, race-clean, and awaiting merge.

The milestones.

M1, server-side brain store. Content-addressed and authz-gated, encrypted at rest. Every artifact gets a fresh per-object key, AES-256-GCM, KMS-wrapped, bound to the repo and artifact, with crypto-shred of the key on retract so a removed fact becomes provably unreadable.

M2, sync protocol over checkpoint\_remote and entiredb. Durable facts sync under compare-and-swap on the branch head. The tenancy key is the injective slug@ULID, a lost race returns 412, and every advance appends to a tamper-evident hash-chained log.

M3, multi-machine shared query. A remote MCP transport over HTTP, so a teammate's agent queries the shared brain without a local clone. The facts tools serve now. Direction: this endpoint becomes the backend of a brain surface on entirehq/mcp (the one hosted connector), not a second standalone connector.

M4, auth and tenancy. Multi-tenant isolation on the org, project, repo SpiceDB cascade, with two independent fail-closed layers.

What P1 rides and reuses (locked in after the landscape review).

Transport: entirehq/mcp. James's hosted connector already solves OAuth, per-principal token exchange, tenancy, and discovery for about 60 tools. The brain registers a tool surface there; M3's endpoint is that surface's backend. No second connector, no duplicate auth plumbing.

Storage direction: EntireDB. Blobs onto objstore, the fact CAS onto refstore, the audit log onto rsl, aligned with the git-meta move. This work is owned in decentralized-architecture, with the brain as its first customer and forcing function. The organizing rule: the brain owns the what and the when; decentralized-architecture owns the shared rails, because a capability with many consumers lives with the platform, not inside one product.

Encryption honesty. Per-object DEKs and crypto-shred exist because the current store is one bucket shared across tenants (separate orgs). In-repo or in EntireDB under the repo's own trust boundary, that need mostly falls away, so the crypto layer is a property of where the data sits, not of the data.

Hardening state. Both PRs went through a 4-angle cleanup pass (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude): one shared AWS store builder, no double-hashing on the publish path, narrowed validation interface, egress-toggle warning parity with the CLI. Trail re-review pending on the latest push.

Links. [entire-api PR \#242](https://github.com/entirehq/entire-api/pull/242) is the store, sync, remote MCP, and tenancy, roughly +8,532 lines. [entire-brain PR \#65](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/65) is the client wire fixes. [Trail \#243](https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-api/trails/243) is entire.io's own AI review, with 0 open findings and risk around 62%.

Where the storage is headed. The brain is in-repo by design already, keyed by repo, branch, and commit, and the hosted service exists only for the shared, authed query that a file in one clone cannot serve. The store rides the session-share stack today (S3 plus KMS) because that was the fastest proven path to ship P1, but the target is to push it down into EntireDB so it inherits resiliency and replication for free: the artifact blobs onto objstore, the fact-set CAS onto refstore, the audit log onto rsl. The one piece EntireDB does not cover yet is encryption at rest with a per-object key and crypto-shred, and that only matters because the current store is shared across tenants, meaning separate orgs in one bucket. In-repo, under the repo's own trust boundary, that need mostly falls away, so the direction is to ride EntireDB and add per-object encrypt and shred there only if a shared store still requires it.

### ð Shipping P1, staging to production

The path is staging-first and reversible, so nothing turns on by accident.

Merge [PR \#242](https://github.com/entirehq/entire-api/pull/242) and [PR \#65](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/65) into main, one approval each.

Staging deploys automatically. The brain migrations (brain\_deks, brain\_overlay\_branches, brain\_fact\_refs, brain\_fact\_advances) apply on deploy and are additive only.

Enable on staging. Set ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_HOSTED\_ENABLED=true on the US and EU staging cells.

Smoke test on partial.to. Publish a brain, advance a fact-set under CAS, and read it back over the remote MCP transport.

Promote to production. Set the same one env var on the US and EU prod cells. That is the activation.

Rollback is instant. Unset the flag and every endpoint fails closed to 503, with data left sealed and dormant.

The only new setting is ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_HOSTED\_ENABLED=true. Everything else is reused, since the brain shares session-share's already-live ENTIRE\_SNAPSHOT\_CIPHER=aws, its S3 bucket, and its KMS key, so there is no new bucket, key, IAM policy, or AWS credential. Until the flag is set, the endpoints fail closed to 503, so merging ships the code dormant on production.

## ðº️ The landscape: what already exists, and how the plan converges it

Four systems already live in this space. The plan does not route around them, it converges onto them. This is grounded in a full read of each codebase.

entirehq/mcp (James). A hosted, multi-tenant, stateless remote MCP proxy: about 60 tools over four upstreams, Streamable HTTP, OAuth resource server with per-principal token exchange, all authorization downstream in SpiceDB. It stores nothing. It is the one hosted MCP transport, and it is architected to add tool surfaces. Decision: the brain does not ship its own standalone MCP connector. The hosted brain is an upstream data service, exposed as a brain surface on this server. P1.M3's transport work becomes the backend that surface calls.

librarian (Alex). A knowledge-indexing and hybrid-search service over team communications and docs: Slack threads, Linear issues, GitHub PRs and issues, markdown. Postgres plus pgvector, its own 768-dim embedding stack (nomic-embed-text on Ollama), RRF fusion, no S3, no code, no sessions. Its roadmap heads toward an entity graph and synthesized views over the same checkpoint stream the brain distills. Librarian is the who-and-why half of team memory (comms); the brain is the what-and-where half (code, keyed to git). The facts and synthesis layer must be negotiated between the two, plus Alisha's MemoryRecords, before either builds further.

entire-search (Alisha, deployed, serves entire.io search today). Product-entity search: checkpoint transcript chunks, commits, PRs. Cohere embed-v4.0 (1536-dim) with vectors in Turbopuffer, BM25 plus ANN with a tier system, SpiceDB ACL fan-out. It deliberately strips code before indexing. Near-zero overlap with the brain: different corpus, different store. The seam is checkpoints, which both consume; a distilled brain fact is a better search document than a raw transcript chunk, a future feed-in, not a conflict.

peregrine (Evis, staging, prod target July). Trigram lexical code search, the Zoekt replacement: regex and full-text over source at platform scale, one index file per repo on S3, plus a tree-sitter symbol layer (15 languages, definition and reference extraction, query-time go-to-def). Zero embeddings. The one real duplication in the landscape: entire-sem and peregrine both maintain per-language tree-sitter extractors. Peregrine has no typed relation graph (its only edge is an untyped ref-to-def link) while entire-sem emits a 30-type relation graph (CALLS, EXTENDS, IMPLEMENTS, DATA\_FLOWS). Peregrine reserved explicit extension slots (SymbolSource::Scip, SymbolPrecision::Semantic) for a higher-precision external symbol producer. Decision to pursue: entire-sem feeds peregrine's symbol overlay, one extractor serving both, with peregrine the find-text-fast engine and the brain the understand-structure engine.

Alisha's MemoryRecords (Agent Improvement Engine). The sharpest overlap in the company: it derives memory from the same checkpoint stream the brain distills facts from, the descriptive and prescriptive halves of one problem. It also sits directly under the P5 north star (prompt quality, fit, routing), and Alisha owns the deployed semantic search too, so she holds two seats at the convergence table. Decision: align with Alisha before building the facts layer or P5 further; P5 should merge efforts, not add a third parallel one.

The score that motivates P2: four search systems live or half-live, three embedding backbones (Cohere 1536, nomic 768, and none), and at least two tree-sitter extractors. P2's converge-code-search RFD ([COR-786](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-786/decision-rfd-converge-code-search-on-one-engine-deprecate-duplicates)) and one-backbone milestone ([COR-788](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-788/unify-knowledge-code-artifact-indexes-on-one-embedding-backbone)) are exactly this cleanup.

## ð£ P2, unified memory, one MCP surface

What it is. The chokepoint. Today retrieval and knowledge are fragmented across several parallel code-search efforts and two parallel knowledge systems. P2 converges them into one shared memory on one embedding backbone, exposed through MCP, so every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Droid, Cursor, Gemini) queries the same thing with the same tools. The gate is P1 transport plus auth, and it is the surface every downstream tool registers on. Done when one MCP tool returns unified results across code and knowledge, and only one search engine and one embedding backbone remain in production.

Tracked in Linear: [Unified, Pluggable Agent Memory](https://linear.app/entirehq/project/unified-pluggable-agent-memory-eaf5762e7339) (High, compressed target Sep to Nov 2026).

M1, converge code-search into one engine (target 2026-09-30). [COR-786](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-786/decision-rfd-converge-code-search-on-one-engine-deprecate-duplicates) is the RFD that picks one direction, and [COR-787](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-787/ship-the-converged-code-search-service) ships the converged code-search service.

M2, converge knowledge into one backbone (target 2026-10-31). [COR-788](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-788/unify-knowledge-code-artifact-indexes-on-one-embedding-backbone) unifies the knowledge and code-artifact indexes on one embedding backbone.

M3, expose brain plus code-search plus knowledge behind one MCP surface (target 2026-11-30). [COR-789](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-789/single-mcp-shared-memory-tool-over-code-knowledge-semantic-index) is the single MCP shared-memory tool.

M4, retire duplicates and prove no regression. [COR-790](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-790/retire-duplicate-search-and-knowledge-paths) decommissions the superseded search and knowledge paths once the unified surface is in production.

## ð¡ Reasoning capture and compounding memory

What it is. The companion to P2 that makes memory compound. Agents capture transcripts, not reasoning, and the reasoning surfaces we have emit prose that gets overwritten, so understanding restarts every run. This captures agent reasoning as structured, queryable facts written back into shared memory, so a later run inherits what an earlier one learned. It rides on the unified surface and the keystone entity deltas. Done when a second agent run reuses the first run's structured reasoning rather than re-deriving it, and a provenance query returns the decision cascade.

Tracked in Linear: [Reasoning Capture and Compounding Memory](https://linear.app/entirehq/project/reasoning-capture-and-compounding-memory-db95c0b2ef1c) (High, target Oct to Dec 2026).

[COR-791](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-791/design-the-structured-reasoning-record-schema-rfd) designs the schema, [COR-792](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-792/persist-reasoning-records-per-checkpointtrail) persists a record per checkpoint and trail.

## ð  P3, coordinated agents

What it is. Let fleets of agents build in parallel without colliding. Today agents cannot coordinate, so two agents editing the same function silently collide. P3 adds entity-level ownership, conflict detection before merge, structured handovers, and a scheduler over ready tasks. The gate is P1 durable state plus the P2 one surface, and it runs in parallel with P4. Done when two agents editing the same entity get a pre-merge conflict warning, a ready task auto-dispatches, and a handover auto-hydrates into the next agent's context.

[COR-795](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-795/spike-evaluate-the-coordination-substrate-task-dag-handovers) evaluates the substrate, [COR-796](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-796/entity-level-claimlease-primitive-claim-a-symbol-expiry) builds the claim primitive so an agent claims a symbol rather than a whole file, with expiry and sweep.

M3, signed handovers and auto-hydration (target 2027-01-31). [COR-798](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-798/structured-handover-schema-mcp-auto-hydration) makes handovers structured data the next agent auto-loads via MCP.

## ð´ P4, cross-repo federation

What it is. Break the repo boundary. Git-native discovery stops at the repo edge, so an agent cannot find who reasoned about similar code elsewhere, and there is no registry to route a task to the right agent. P4 shares reasoning across repos and orgs, and adds a capability registry so tasks route by capability. The gate is P1 durable state plus the P2 one surface, and it runs in parallel with P3. Done when an agent working in repo A surfaces relevant reasoning from repo B, and tasks route to an agent by declared capability.

Tracked in Linear: [Cross-Repo Shared Reasoning](https://linear.app/entirehq/project/cross-repo-shared-reasoning-0f9532a0d661) (Medium, compressed target Jan to Mar 2027).

M1, cross-repo semantic index and query (target 2027-02-28). [COR-801](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-801/cross-repo-semantic-discovery-over-the-federated-index) queries the semantic index across repos over the federated index and mirror pipeline.

M2, cross-org authz. [COR-802](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-802/spike-cross-org-authz-for-shared-reasoning) defines the authorization model for sharing reasoning across orgs, building on the existing MCP and SpiceDB gating.

M3, agent capability registry (target 2027-03-31). [COR-803](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-803/agent-capability-registry-discovery) registers agents by capability so a task resolves to the best-fit agent.

## ⭐ P5, behavioral intelligence: the north star

What it is. The payoff the whole arc builds toward: turn retained behavior into decisions. Every prompt, session, and outcome is already captured as checkpoints; P5 mines that record. It came from the Salesforce ask and it is what makes the memory layer a product, not plumbing. The gate is the P2 one surface plus P3 coordinated execution.

What it delivers.

Prompt intelligence. Score a prompt's quality before it runs, from retained outcome signal. See which people write prompts that succeed. Surface a curated best-prompt library of exemplars mined from real checkpoints, so the org's best prompting becomes everyone's baseline.

Fit modeling. Who, or which agent or model, succeeds on what kind of task, from history instead of vibes.

Auto-routing. Send a task to the agent or person most likely to do it well, with P4's capability registry supplying the candidates.

Feedback loop and org dashboards. Outcomes flow back into the models; leadership watches the org learn.

Alignment first. Alisha's MemoryRecords (Agent Improvement Engine) mines the same checkpoint stream toward the same territory, and she owns the deployed semantic search. P5 starts with a merge-of-efforts conversation, not a third parallel build. The brain brings what the others lack: facts with provenance anchors tied to commits, and brain-bench's eval discipline as the pattern for scoring the prompt-quality classifier.

Tracked in Linear: [P5 · Behavioral Intelligence (North Star)](https://linear.app/entirehq/project/p5-behavioral-intelligence-north-star-1bb9991bc853) (High, target Jan to Jun 2027).

M1, prompt-quality classifier (target 2027-02-28): score prompts from outcome signal (checkpoint success, iteration count, review outcomes).

M2, per-person profiles and the best-prompt library (target 2027-03-31): which employees write prompts that succeed, and the best of their prompts, curated from real checkpoints.

M3, agent and person to task fit (target 2027-04-30): the fit model over checkpoint history.

M4, auto-routing (target 2027-05-31): route work to the best-fit agent or person.

M5, feedback loop and org dashboards (target 2027-06-30): close the loop, show the learning.

## Architecture decisions

ADR-1, schema freeze. The brain wire schema is major.minor, additive minors, tolerant readers. From P0.

ADR-P1-A, opt-in egress. Hosted publish is never implicit. It is gated on an explicit entire brain publish plus ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_ALLOW\_HOSTED.

ADR-P1-C, branch build model. A default push builds a baseline, a feature branch builds an overlay, merge promotes it, delete garbage-collects it.

ADR-P1-D, platform target. The post-refactor mirror and decentralized architecture. Treat interfaces as a moving target. The intent is for the brain store to ride entiredb (objstore for blobs, refstore for the fact CAS, rsl for the audit log), with per-object encryption and crypto-shred as the one capability that still needs a home.

## Critical path

P0 finishes the brain. P1 is the linchpin, since store, sync, query, and auth unblock everything else. The keystone semantic index and unified memory land next, and the P2 single MCP surface is the chokepoint every downstream tool registers on. Reasoning capture builds on the record schema and the unified surface. Coordinated agents and cross-repo federation both need P1 plus the one surface, and they run in parallel.

# The brain roadmap, phase by phase

The arc in one line: **make one brain → share it → make it the only memory → make it compound → coordinate fleets on it → cross repo walls → turn it all into decisions.**

---

## 🟢 P0 — GA the local brain *(✅ done, closed 08-15)*
**The foundation.** The local brain already worked; P0 was making it something the rest can *depend* on — not new build, but freeze-and-tag.

- **entire-graph** (was entire-sem): parses code into symbols + a 30-type relation graph (CALLS, EXTENDS, DATA_FLOWS…) with tree-sitter. Zero vectors.
- **entire-brain**: durable, branch-scoped, provenance-anchored facts + ~33 local MCP tools agents query.
- **GraphMark** (was brain-bench): the CI regression gate across ~30 languages.

What "done" meant: schema frozen (additive-only 1.x), both repos tagged v0.1.0, MCP contract locked, benchmark wired as a required floor, install docs. All 11 gates read ✅ on main today.

**Why it's first:** every later phase trusts this contract. You can't share, converge, or mine a thing whose schema still moves.

---

## 🔵 P1 — Shared / hosted brain *(built + wire-verified, awaiting merge)*
**The differentiator.** Lift the brain off the laptop: one member's agent learns something, every teammate's agent can read it.

- **M1** server-side store — content-addressed, encrypted per-object (AES-256-GCM, KMS-wrapped), **crypto-shred** on retract so a removed fact is provably unreadable
- **M2** sync — read-merge-CAS on a branch head; lost race = 412, re-read, re-merge; tamper-evident hash-chained audit log
- **M3** remote MCP query — a teammate queries the shared brain with no local clone
- **M4** auth/tenancy — SpiceDB org→project→repo cascade, fail-closed twice

Key design rule (ADR-P1-E): **the merge runs on the runner, never the server.** The server stores bytes and moves pointers. That rule is exactly what the wire reconciliation I just did restored — the api side had drifted into server-side merging.

Current truth: client (#85) and server (#242) agree on the wire, live round-trip passes, activation is one env var (`ENTIRE_BRAIN_HOSTED_ENABLED=true`), rollback is unsetting it. Needs merges.

---

## 🧩 Keystone — semantic index tied to VCS *(between P1 and P2)*
Not a "P" but the hinge: persist **entity deltas onto checkpoints** and build a git-native index, so "which checkpoints changed entity X?" is answered from the index, not by re-parsing. Ties meaning to git history permanently. Everything from P2 on assumes this exists.

---

## 🟣 P2 — Unified memory, one MCP surface *(Sep–Nov 2026)*
**The chokepoint.** Today the company runs **4 search systems** (brain, entire-search, librarian, peregrine), **3 embedding backbones** (Cohere-1536, nomic-768, none), and **2+ tree-sitter extractors**. P2 collapses that:

- **M1** one code-search engine — the mechanism already exists: entire-graph exports SCIP (#97), peregrine reserved the `SymbolSource::Scip` slot. One extractor feeds both; peregrine = find-text-fast, brain = understand-structure
- **M2** one embedding backbone for knowledge — though #104's result (beating mem0 with *zero* embeddings) suggests the real answer may be "fewer embeddings," worth deciding with data
- **M3** one MCP tool over code + knowledge + brain — every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Droid, Gemini) queries the *same* memory
- **M4** retire the duplicates

**Why it matters:** it's the surface everything downstream registers on. No convergence → every later phase multiplies the fragmentation.

---

## 🟡 Reasoning capture *(companion to P2, Oct–Dec 2026)*
**Makes memory compound.** Agents capture transcripts, not reasoning — so understanding restarts every run. This writes agent reasoning back as **structured, queryable facts**: a record schema per checkpoint/trail, review findings written back as durable facts, and a provenance graph (decision → task → PR → review).

Done when: a second run *reuses* the first run's reasoning instead of re-deriving it.

---

## 🟠 P3 — Coordinated agents *(Nov 2026–Feb 2027)*
**Fleets without collisions.** Two agents editing the same function today collide silently.

- **entity-level claims/leases** — claim a *symbol*, not a file, with expiry
- **pre-merge conflict detection** — warned before the merge, not after
- **signed handovers** — structured data the next agent auto-hydrates via MCP
- **scheduler** — ready tasks auto-dispatch to sandboxes; presence/read-receipts so a dead claim gets reclaimed

Gate: P1's durable state + P2's one surface. Runs parallel with P4.

---

## 🔴 P4 — Cross-repo federation *(Jan–Mar 2027)*
**Break the repo wall.** An agent in repo A surfaces reasoning from repo B; a capability registry routes tasks to the best-fit agent. Cross-org authz rides the existing SpiceDB/MCP gating. Parallel with P3.

---

## ⭐ P5 — Behavioral intelligence *(north star, Jan–Jun 2027)*
**The payoff: retained behavior becomes decisions.** Every prompt, session, and outcome is already captured as checkpoints — P5 mines it:

- **prompt intelligence** — score a prompt before it runs; a best-prompt library mined from real checkpoints so the org's best prompting becomes everyone's baseline
- **fit modeling** — who/which agent succeeds on what, from history not vibes
- **auto-routing** — send work to the best-fit agent or person
- **org dashboards** — leadership watches the org learn

Came from the Salesforce ask; it's what makes the memory layer a *product*. Explicit first step: merge efforts with Alisha's MemoryRecords (same checkpoint stream, same territory) rather than building a third parallel system.

---

## The logic of the ordering
```
P0 trust the contract
 └─ P1 share it            ← the linchpin; everything needs durable shared state
     └─ keystone: tie meaning to git
         └─ P2 one surface  ← the chokepoint; all tools register here
             ├─ reasoning capture (compound)
             ├─ P3 coordinate ┐ parallel
             └─ P4 federate  ┘
                 └─ P5 decisions (north star)
```
Governing constraint throughout: **no new infrastructure** — everything rides entiredb, checkpoint_remote, snapshotstore/crypt, SpiceDB, the jurisdiction forwarder.

Where you actually are: **P0 done, P1 one approval away, keystone unstarted (its Linear issues are canceled — needs reactivating), P2's M1 mechanism already half-built.**

content.text:
The `distill` command's own help line states the fault line: `"Distill captured sessions into durable facts (agent-required)"` — the only agent-dependent step in the whole stack.

## What Thomas is actually pointing at

**Surface problem:** "the brain" is one product in the user's head but three separately-invoked setup paths in reality:

1. **Brain without agent** — the deterministic layer: code graph + index/embeddings/recall. Seconds, free, no LLM, works on any repo immediately.
2. **Brain with agent** — the same brain but with LLM-backed enrichment wired in.
3. **Facts extraction** — `distill`, which chews through **captured session history** to produce durable facts. This is agent-required, costs tokens, and its runtime is proportional to how many sessions the repo already has.

Three entry points, three mental models, no single funnel. That's the "confusing" part, and your wizard idea fixes exactly that part.

**The deeper problem — Thomas's objection to the wizard:** onboarding conflates a **fast, bounded** step with a **slow, unbounded** one. Distill time scales with the session backlog, so on any repo with real history it "runs long" no matter how nice the terminal UX is. A wizard can reorder and rename steps; it can't make an O(sessions) LLM pass fit inside a synchronous setup flow. That's why he says "unless the repo has no or few sessions yet" — a fresh repo is the only case where the three paths collapse into one quick flow naturally.

## The resolution shape (if you want a reply to him)

The answer isn't "make setup one blocking flow," it's **split by latency class**:

- **Synchronous onboarding = the deterministic core only.** Graph + index, done in seconds, brain is immediately queryable. This is already the reality in devenv — the graph is built everywhere, facts only where distill has run — onboarding just doesn't present it that way.
- **Distill = background backfill, never a setup gate.** Kick it off from the wizard but return the prompt immediately; process **newest sessions first** (recency-weighted, so the useful facts land early), backfill the tail opportunistically, and let `doctor`/`brain_status` be the progress surface ("facts: 120/900 sessions distilled").

So the wizard promise becomes *"usable in 30 seconds, gets smarter over the next hour"* instead of *"wait for everything."* That concedes Thomas's point (the agent pass will always run long) while keeping yours (one clean funnel) — the fix is making the slow part invisible, not fast.

**Yes — your fix is the right shape, and most of it already exists in the brain.** I checked the repo: the pieces Thomas thinks need inventing are largely built, so your Slack answer can be "package what's there," not "design a daemon."

What's already in `entire-brain`:

- **`hook session-end --session <id>`** (`internal/cli/hook_cmd.go:62`) — per-session incremental distill wired to the session-lifecycle hook. Its own comment states the design: batch distill is expensive and forgotten, so the hook distills *just the ended session*, may legitimately take minutes and spend tokens because nobody is waiting, and "correctness never depends on it firing." This kills Thomas's "people probably forget to run it" — there's nothing to remember; capture already fires the hook.
- **`watch`** (`internal/cli/watch.go:121`) — "Keep the brain fresh automatically (deterministic refresh is free; agent steps are gated)." That's the daemon-shaped thing, already scoped correctly.

So the answers to the three open questions in the thread:

**1. Does background-with-updates fix it?** It fixes the *onboarding* half, but only if you split by latency class: setup runs the deterministic core synchronously (graph + index, seconds, brain immediately queryable) and kicks the agent backfill in the background, **newest sessions first** so useful facts land early. The *steady-state* half — Thomas's real follow-up — is already fixed by the session-end hook: after backfill, distill is event-driven per session, bounded to one session's work. The O(all-sessions) problem exists exactly once, at onboarding, and it runs behind the prompt.

**2. What's the role of a daemon, then?** Almost nothing — that's the point. Steady state needs no resident process because the trigger is event-driven (session end). What's left for a "daemon" is just *scheduling the backfill and catch-up* (repos that were cold, hooks that didn't fire), and the proven pattern for that is `git maintenance`: a per-repo registry plus one launchd/cron schedule — a singular scheduler, not a singular resident daemon. And Thomas's "singular brain daemon across all repos" instinct is actually right *long-term*, but the answer is the **hosted brain (P1)**: entire-api already runs an agent worker server-side (checkpoint-analysis in `cmd/repo-activity`), so hosted distillation on the cell is where "one daemon for all repos" naturally lives. A local daemon would be a stopgap for a problem the roadmap already solves.

**3. "Is it the hard diff problem?"** No. Sessions are append-only with stable ids, and the hook's incremental cache already makes re-processing a seen session free — incremental distill is a watermark over an append-only log, which is easy. The genuinely hard part is **policy, not diffing**: whose API tokens the background agent spends, when it's allowed to run, and concurrency caps — which is exactly why `watch` gates the agent steps while keeping deterministic refresh free.

Your proposed UX holds up as-is: terminal setup → deterministic brain usable in seconds → backfill in background → `doctor`/status as the progress surface ("facts: 120/900 sessions distilled"). The one thing I'd add when you reply to Thomas: frame the wizard as *installing the hooks + registering the repo for maintenance*, not as running the extraction. Then "the agent stuff runs long" stops being an onboarding problem at all — it's a background property the user watches, and eventually a server-side one.

Here's the plan with it in:

---

**Brain onboarding plan**

**One command: `entire brain setup`**

1. **Instant (seconds, blocking):** build the code graph + index. Brain usable immediately — no agent, no tokens.
2. **Backfill (background):** start fact extraction over past sessions, newest first, so useful facts land early. Setup returns the prompt right away.
3. **The daemon — mostly built (`workspace watch`):** setup registers the repo into the workspace and makes sure one `workspace watch` daemon is running (launchd/systemd). One daemon covers **all** repos:
   - free deterministic refresh on every change (sessions, index, overlay)
   - agent work (distill/seed) gated: at most once per interval, budget-capped, cheap model, cursor persisted so restarts never double-spend
4. **Per-session freshness:** the session-end hook distills each session as it ends — already built. Between daemon and hook, nobody ever has to remember to run anything.
5. **Progress:** `entire brain status` shows "facts: 120/900 sessions distilled." Doctor stays the health check.

**Pitch:** setup = usable in 30 seconds + registered with the one brain daemon. The agent work still runs long — but in the background, budget-gated, across every repo, and nobody waits on it or has to remember it. Long-term the same daemon role moves server-side with the hosted brain (P1).

---

What's genuinely new to build is small: the `setup` wizard itself, daemon install/registration glue (launchd/systemd unit), and the backfill progress counter in `status`. The watch loop, workspace registry, token gating, and session-end hook are already in the repo.

Short answer: **the backfill is just `distill` run over the session backlog — it uses whatever coding agent is already on the machine, with the user's own auth.** Nothing new.

Breaking that down:

- **Input:** the captured session transcripts the repo already has (`.git/entire-sessions/` exports / checkpoint history). That's the raw material.
- **Free part first:** export + overlay + index of those transcripts is deterministic — zero tokens. That happens instantly during setup.
- **Token-spending part:** fact extraction shells out to an agent CLI on PATH — default is `codex`, `claude` also supported — pinned to a **cheap model + low reasoning effort** via the existing `--model`/`--effort` flags. It runs under the developer's own subscription/API key, same as running distill by hand today.
- **Cost guardrails (already built into watch):** `--budget` caps total agent runs, `--distill-every` rate-limits, and the persisted cursor means a restart never re-spends on sessions already done. Newest-first ordering means the most valuable facts land in the first few minutes even if the tail takes hours.
- **Long-term:** once the hosted brain (P1) is live, backfill can move server-side — the cell already runs an Anthropic-backed worker for checkpoint analysis, so the same pattern gives you org-paid, server-side extraction and no local agent dependency at all.

So the honest framing for Thomas: backfill costs the user their own agent tokens on a cheap model, budget-capped, in the background — and that cost disappears to the server side once hosted lands.

(Meanwhile the three Keystone scouts are still running in the background — I'll come back with the plan + questions when they report.)

{"fileContent":"# ð§  The Semantic Reasoning Layer: Roadmap

Turn the local brain into a shared reasoning substrate that a fleet of agents builds on. Git preserves change, but it does not preserve meaning. This initiative gives every agent persistent, shared, pluggable memory tied to git history, so humans and agents can reason and build in parallel without colliding.

Initiative: [Semantic Reasoning Layer](https://linear.app/entirehq/initiative/semantic-reasoning-layer-e043385c2167) (Linear, Active) · Vision: [entire.io/vision](https://entire.io/vision) · As of: July 2026

The arc: ð¢ P0 finish the brain, then ðµ P1 host it, then ð£ P2 unify memory behind one surface, then ð  P3 coordinate fleets and ð´ P4 federate across repos in parallel, all feeding ⭐ P5, the north star: behavioral intelligence, where retained behavior becomes decisions (best-agent routing, prompt quality per person, a best-prompt library).

Governing constraint: no new infrastructure. The whole arc rides entire.io's existing rails (entiredb, checkpoint\_remote, snapshotstore and snapshotcrypt, authz and SpiceDB, the jurisdiction forwarder). Each milestone ports proven parts onto the brain model rather than building storage or crypto from scratch.

## ð Timeline at a glance

Target: the whole roadmap complete by end of March 2027. The schedule below is the compressed plan to hit that date. The dates run tight and in parallel from P2 onward.

| Phase | Focus | Window | Status |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| ð¢ P0 GA the local brain | Harden entire-sem, brain, MCP surface, bench | Jul to Aug 2026 | Ships today, GA wrapper in progress |
| ðµ P1 Shared / hosted brain | Server store, sync, remote query, auth | Now, ship Aug 2026 | Built and tested on clones, one step from prod |
| ð§© Keystone: semantic index tied to VCS | Entity deltas, git-native index, causality | Aug to Sep 2026 | Planned |
| ð£ P2 Unified memory, one MCP surface | Converge search, one backbone, one surface | Sep to Nov 2026 | Planned |
| ð¡ Reasoning capture, compounding memory | Record schema, write-back, provenance graph | Oct to Dec 2026 | Planned |
| ð  P3 Coordinated agents | Claims, conflict detection, handovers, scheduler | Nov 2026 to Feb 2027 | Planned |
| ð´ P4 Cross-repo federation | Federated discovery, capability registry | Jan to Mar 2027 | Planned |
| ⭐ P5 Behavioral intelligence (north star) | Prompt quality, best-prompt library, fit, auto-routing | Jan to Jun 2027 | Planned |

The March 2027 target covers the enabling phases (P0 through P4). The P5 north star starts as soon as P2's surface and P3's coordination land, and runs to June 2027. Linear milestone dates now match the compressed schedule.

## ð¢ P0, GA the local brain

What it is. The foundation the whole initiative stands on. The local brain already runs, so P0 is finish work and release hygiene, not new build. There is no gate here. Everything ships today, but nothing is formally tagged, so P0 is the wrapper that makes it something the rest of the arc can depend on.

The pieces, all live today.

entire-sem is the semantic provider. It parses code into symbols and relations with tree-sitter, and it uses no vectors anywhere in the stack.

entire-brain is the local brain. It holds durable, branch-scoped, provenance-anchored facts, plus a local MCP surface of about 33 tools that agents query.

brain-bench is the CI gate. It benchmarks the extractor against a reference tool across roughly 30 languages and fails the build on regression or drift.

The milestones.

M1, harden and GA entire-sem. Version-stamp it and freeze the schema so everything downstream can trust the contract.

M2, close the brain blockers. Ship the local brain with honest claims, no overreach.

M3, GA the MCP surface for both plugins. Harden the local tool surface for the Claude Code and Codex plugins.

M4, brain-bench as the automated eval gate. Make the benchmark a required regression floor.

M5, release logistics. The release checklist, the compatibility matrix, and distribution.

Foundation build tracked in Linear: [Semantic Index Tied to VCS History](https://linear.app/entirehq/project/semantic-index-tied-to-vcs-history-ea453fa387e2) (Urgent). This is the piece that persists entity-level meaning onto checkpoints and a git-native index, so meaning is stored with git history and not re-parsed on demand. Done when entire and MCP can answer "which checkpoints changed entity X" from the index.

Entity deltas in checkpoint metadata (target 2026-08-15): [COR-781](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-781/spike-map-semantic-extractor-snapshot-checkpoint-metadata-schema) spike the schema, then [COR-782](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-782/embed-entity-deltas-into-the-checkpoint-metadata-write-path) embed the deltas into the write path.

Git-native entity to checkpoint index (target 2026-09-15): [COR-783](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-783/build-the-git-native-entity-checkpoint-index) build the index, [COR-784](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-784/mcp-tool-query-checkpointssessions-by-semantic-entity) expose it as an MCP tool.

Transparency-log semantic causality (target 2026-09-30): [COR-785](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-785/tie-transparency-log-events-to-semantic-causality) tie ref-change events to the session and entities that caused them.

## ðµ P1, shared / hosted brain ⭐

What it is. The differentiator. P1 lifts the brain off the laptop into a shared, server-side, multi-tenant service, so one member's agent learns something and every other member's agent can read it. The gate is the P0 schema-freeze plus a namespace, and it deliberately relaxes the local-only guardrail. All four parts are built and DB-tested on clone branches, race-clean, and awaiting merge.

The milestones.

M1, server-side brain store. Content-addressed and authz-gated, encrypted at rest. Every artifact gets a fresh per-object key, AES-256-GCM, KMS-wrapped, bound to the repo and artifact, with crypto-shred of the key on retract so a removed fact becomes provably unreadable.

M2, sync protocol over checkpoint\_remote and entiredb. Durable facts sync under compare-and-swap on the branch head. The tenancy key is the injective slug@ULID, a lost race returns 412, and every advance appends to a tamper-evident hash-chained log.

M3, multi-machine shared query. A remote MCP transport over HTTP, so a teammate's agent queries the shared brain without a local clone. The facts tools serve now. Direction: this endpoint becomes the backend of a brain surface on entirehq/mcp (the one hosted connector), not a second standalone connector.

M4, auth and tenancy. Multi-tenant isolation on the org, project, repo SpiceDB cascade, with two independent fail-closed layers.

What P1 rides and reuses (locked in after the landscape review).

Transport: entirehq/mcp. James's hosted connector already solves OAuth, per-principal token exchange, tenancy, and discovery for about 60 tools. The brain registers a tool surface there; M3's endpoint is that surface's backend. No second connector, no duplicate auth plumbing.

Storage direction: EntireDB. Blobs onto objstore, the fact CAS onto refstore, the audit log onto rsl, aligned with the git-meta move. This work is owned in decentralized-architecture, with the brain as its first customer and forcing function. The organizing rule: the brain owns the what and the when; decentralized-architecture owns the shared rails, because a capability with many consumers lives with the platform, not inside one product.

Encryption honesty. Per-object DEKs and crypto-shred exist because the current store is one bucket shared across tenants (separate orgs). In-repo or in EntireDB under the repo's own trust boundary, that need mostly falls away, so the crypto layer is a property of where the data sits, not of the data.

Hardening state. Both PRs went through a 4-angle cleanup pass (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude): one shared AWS store builder, no double-hashing on the publish path, narrowed validation interface, egress-toggle warning parity with the CLI. Trail re-review pending on the latest push.

Links. [entire-api PR \#242](https://github.com/entirehq/entire-api/pull/242) is the store, sync, remote MCP, and tenancy, roughly +8,532 lines. [entire-brain PR \#65](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/65) is the client wire fixes. [Trail \#243](https://entire.io/gh/entirehq/entire-api/trails/243) is entire.io's own AI review, with 0 open findings and risk around 62%.

Where the storage is headed. The brain is in-repo by design already, keyed by repo, branch, and commit, and the hosted service exists only for the shared, authed query that a file in one clone cannot serve. The store rides the session-share stack today (S3 plus KMS) because that was the fastest proven path to ship P1, but the target is to push it down into EntireDB so it inherits resiliency and replication for free: the artifact blobs onto objstore, the fact-set CAS onto refstore, the audit log onto rsl. The one piece EntireDB does not cover yet is encryption at rest with a per-object key and crypto-shred, and that only matters because the current store is shared across tenants, meaning separate orgs in one bucket. In-repo, under the repo's own trust boundary, that need mostly falls away, so the direction is to ride EntireDB and add per-object encrypt and shred there only if a shared store still requires it.

### ð Shipping P1, staging to production

The path is staging-first and reversible, so nothing turns on by accident.

Merge [PR \#242](https://github.com/entirehq/entire-api/pull/242) and [PR \#65](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/65) into main, one approval each.

Staging deploys automatically. The brain migrations (brain\_deks, brain\_overlay\_branches, brain\_fact\_refs, brain\_fact\_advances) apply on deploy and are additive only.

Enable on staging. Set ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_HOSTED\_ENABLED=true on the US and EU staging cells.

Smoke test on partial.to. Publish a brain, advance a fact-set under CAS, and read it back over the remote MCP transport.

Promote to production. Set the same one env var on the US and EU prod cells. That is the activation.

Rollback is instant. Unset the flag and every endpoint fails closed to 503, with data left sealed and dormant.

The only new setting is ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_HOSTED\_ENABLED=true. Everything else is reused, since the brain shares session-share's already-live ENTIRE\_SNAPSHOT\_CIPHER=aws, its S3 bucket, and its KMS key, so there is no new bucket, key, IAM policy, or AWS credential. Until the flag is set, the endpoints fail closed to 503, so merging ships the code dormant on production.

## ðº️ The landscape: what already exists, and how the plan converges it

Four systems already live in this space. The plan does not route around them, it converges onto them. This is grounded in a full read of each codebase.

entirehq/mcp (James). A hosted, multi-tenant, stateless remote MCP proxy: about 60 tools over four upstreams, Streamable HTTP, OAuth resource server with per-principal token exchange, all authorization downstream in SpiceDB. It stores nothing. It is the one hosted MCP transport, and it is architected to add tool surfaces. Decision: the brain does not ship its own standalone MCP connector. The hosted brain is an upstream data service, exposed as a brain surface on this server. P1.M3's transport work becomes the backend that surface calls.

librarian (Alex). A knowledge-indexing and hybrid-search service over team communications and docs: Slack threads, Linear issues, GitHub PRs and issues, markdown. Postgres plus pgvector, its own 768-dim embedding stack (nomic-embed-text on Ollama), RRF fusion, no S3, no code, no sessions. Its roadmap heads toward an entity graph and synthesized views over the same checkpoint stream the brain distills. Librarian is the who-and-why half of team memory (comms); the brain is the what-and-where half (code, keyed to git). The facts and synthesis layer must be negotiated between the two, plus Alisha's MemoryRecords, before either builds further.

entire-search (Alisha, deployed, serves entire.io search today). Product-entity search: checkpoint transcript chunks, commits, PRs. Cohere embed-v4.0 (1536-dim) with vectors in Turbopuffer, BM25 plus ANN with a tier system, SpiceDB ACL fan-out. It deliberately strips code before indexing. Near-zero overlap with the brain: different corpus, different store. The seam is checkpoints, which both consume; a distilled brain fact is a better search document than a raw transcript chunk, a future feed-in, not a conflict.

peregrine (Evis, staging, prod target July). Trigram lexical code search, the Zoekt replacement: regex and full-text over source at platform scale, one index file per repo on S3, plus a tree-sitter symbol layer (15 languages, definition and reference extraction, query-time go-to-def). Zero embeddings. The one real duplication in the landscape: entire-sem and peregrine both maintain per-language tree-sitter extractors. Peregrine has no typed relation graph (its only edge is an untyped ref-to-def link) while entire-sem emits a 30-type relation graph (CALLS, EXTENDS, IMPLEMENTS, DATA\_FLOWS). Peregrine reserved explicit extension slots (SymbolSource::Scip, SymbolPrecision::Semantic) for a higher-precision external symbol producer. Decision to pursue: entire-sem feeds peregrine's symbol overlay, one extractor serving both, with peregrine the find-text-fast engine and the brain the understand-structure engine.

Alisha's MemoryRecords (Agent Improvement Engine). The sharpest overlap in the company: it derives memory from the same checkpoint stream the brain distills facts from, the descriptive and prescriptive halves of one problem. It also sits directly under the P5 north star (prompt quality, fit, routing), and Alisha owns the deployed semantic search too, so she holds two seats at the convergence table. Decision: align with Alisha before building the facts layer or P5 further; P5 should merge efforts, not add a third parallel one.

The score that motivates P2: four search systems live or half-live, three embedding backbones (Cohere 1536, nomic 768, and none), and at least two tree-sitter extractors. P2's converge-code-search RFD ([COR-786](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-786/decision-rfd-converge-code-search-on-one-engine-deprecate-duplicates)) and one-backbone milestone ([COR-788](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-788/unify-knowledge-code-artifact-indexes-on-one-embedding-backbone)) are exactly this cleanup.

## ð£ P2, unified memory, one MCP surface

What it is. The chokepoint. Today retrieval and knowledge are fragmented across several parallel code-search efforts and two parallel knowledge systems. P2 converges them into one shared memory on one embedding backbone, exposed through MCP, so every agent (Claude Code, Codex, Droid, Cursor, Gemini) queries the same thing with the same tools. The gate is P1 transport plus auth, and it is the surface every downstream tool registers on. Done when one MCP tool returns unified results across code and knowledge, and only one search engine and one embedding backbone remain in production.

Tracked in Linear: [Unified, Pluggable Agent Memory](https://linear.app/entirehq/project/unified-pluggable-agent-memory-eaf5762e7339) (High, compressed target Sep to Nov 2026).

M2, converge knowledge into one backbone (target 2026-10-31). [COR-788](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-788/unify-knowledge-code-artifact-indexes-on-one-embedding-backbone) unifies the knowledge and code-artifact indexes on one embedding backbone.

M3, expose brain plus code-search plus knowledge behind one MCP surface (target 2026-11-30). [COR-789](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-789/single-mcp-shared-memory-tool-over-code-knowledge-semantic-index) is the single MCP shared-memory tool.

## ð¡ Reasoning capture and compounding memory

What it is. The companion to P2 that makes memory compound. Agents capture transcripts, not reasoning, and the reasoning surfaces we have emit prose that gets overwritten, so understanding restarts every run. This captures agent reasoning as structured, queryable facts written back into shared memory, so a later run inherits what an earlier one learned. It rides on the unified surface and the keystone entity deltas. Done when a second agent run reuses the first run's structured reasoning rather than re-deriving it, and a provenance query returns the decision cascade.

What it is. Let fleets of agents build in parallel without colliding. Today agents cannot coordinate, so two agents editing the same function silently collide. P3 adds entity-level ownership, conflict detection before merge, structured handovers, and a scheduler over ready tasks. The gate is P1 durable state plus the P2 one surface, and it runs in parallel with P4. What it is. Break the repo boundary. ## Architecture decisions

ADR-1, schema freeze. The brain wire schema is major.minor, additive minors, tolerant readers. From P0.

ADR-P1-A, opt-in egress. Hosted publish is never implicit. It is gated on an explicit entire brain publish plus ENTIRE\_BRAIN\_ALLOW\_HOSTED.

ADR-P1-C, branch build model. A default push builds a baseline, a feature branch builds an overlay, merge promotes it, delete garbage-collects it.

ADR-P1-D, platform target. The post-refactor mirror and decentralized architecture. Treat interfaces as a moving target. The intent is for the brain store to ride entiredb (objstore for blobs, refstore for the fact CAS, rsl for the audit log), with per-object encryption and crypto-shred as the one capability that still needs a home.

## Critical path

P0 finishes the brain. P1 is the linchpin, since store, sync, query, and auth unblock everything else. The keystone semantic index and unified memory land next, and the P2 single MCP surface is the chokepoint every downstream tool registers on. Reasoning capture builds on the record schema and the unified surface. Coordinated agents and cross-repo federation both need P1 plus the one surface, and they run in parallel.

## What the Keystone is, in one sentence

Every checkpoint gets a small record of **which functions/classes/types it changed** ("entity deltas"), plus a reverse index so anyone — CLI or agent via MCP — can ask **"show me every checkpoint that ever touched function X"** and get an instant answer instead of re-parsing git history.

## What the scouts found (why this is very buildable)

- **The delta producer exists**: `entire graph diff` already outputs exactly the needed list (added/removed/modified/renamed per entity). Only gap: its JSON is unversioned — must be stamped before we persist it.
- **The attach point exists**: checkpoints store metadata as JSON files in the checkpoint tree, safely extensible, and the cli already has an async "backfill" pattern (used for attribution stats) we can copy for entity deltas. Base+head SHAs are already in hand at checkpoint time.
- **The index store exists**: brain's git-meta engine supports per-commit keys and list-append ops — the exact shape for an entity→checkpoint index — currently unused for this.
- **Nothing connects them today**: brain never calls `graph diff`; fact provenance anchors to "latest checkpoint at distill time" (coarse), and `why`/`blame` are line-based, not symbol-based. The Keystone is the missing wiring, not new machinery.

## The plan (3 PRs + 1 deferral)

1. **entire-graph PR (tiny):** stamp a `schema_version` on `graph diff` output → this frozen schema *is* the COR-781 spike deliverable.
2. **entire-brain PR (the bulk):** index builder that walks existing checkpoint history, runs `graph diff` per checkpoint, and writes deltas + the reverse entity→checkpoint index. content.text:
Got your first two answers — **build all three PRs in parallel** and **git-meta as source of truth + local cache for speed**.

You didn't answer the COR-785 question and flagged you want to clarify something — what would you like me to explain or reconsider? (If it's COR-785: in plain terms it's the "audit-trail linking" piece — when a ref moves on the server, record *which session and which functions* caused that move. It's server-side, low-priority, and the index works fully without it, which is why I suggested deferring until P1 is merged.)
what is it?

**COR-785 = "make the audit log explain *why*, not just *what*."**

Breaking it down simply:

**What the transparency log is today:** entiredb keeps a tamper-evident, append-only log of every ref change — every time a branch/checkpoint ref moves, there's a signed entry saying "ref X moved from commit A to commit B, at this time, by this identity." Think of it as a security camera on the repo: it records that *something happened*, and nobody can secretly edit the tape.

**What it can't answer:** *why* it happened. The log entry knows "ref moved A→B" but has no idea that this was **session `s-123`, where Claude was fixing the auth bug, and the change touched `verifyToken()` and `SessionStore.refresh()`**. That context exists — the session and the entity deltas both exist — but nothing links them to the log entry.

**What COR-785 does:** attach that link. Each ref-change event gets tied to the session that caused it and the entities it changed. Then you can ask causality questions off the tamper-proof record:

- "Who/what changed `verifyToken()` on main last week?" → *session s-123, agent claude, checkpoint c-456* — answered from the signed log, not from trust.
- "This ref moved at 3am — which agent run did that, and what did it touch?"

**Why it's the natural third piece:** milestone 1 creates the entity deltas, milestone 2 indexes them locally — COR-785 stitches the same information into the *server-side, tamper-evident* record. It's the compliance/security-grade version of the same answer.

**Why I recommended deferring it:** it's the only keystone piece that lives server-side (entiredb/hosted), so it depends on the P1 rails that are still sitting unmerged in #85/#242 — and the keystone's done-when ("which checkpoints changed entity X, from the index") is fully met without it. Building it now means building against a moving target.

Want me to defer it (my recommendation), or include it in this push?
why do we eed this for brain?

Honestly? **The brain doesn't strictly need it — and that's the real answer.**

Separating the two things:

**What the brain genuinely needs is the first two keystone pieces** (deltas + index). Those feed brain features directly:
- Facts get anchored to the checkpoint that *actually* made the change (today it's "whatever the latest checkpoint was when distill ran" — coarse and sometimes wrong).
- Agents get "which checkpoints touched this function" as an MCP tool — real recall improvement.
- P3 literally cannot exist without it: entity claims and pre-merge conflict detection are built on knowing entity→change history.

**COR-785 is not a brain feature — it's a trust feature.** The brain will already know "session s-123 changed `verifyToken()`" from its own index. COR-785 just re-records that same link on the server's tamper-evident log. What that buys:

1. **In a *shared* brain, the client's word isn't enough.** Locally, your own index is trustworthy. Multi-tenant, a claim like "that change came from session X" is just something a client wrote down. The server-side log is the neutral referee.
2. **P5 mines causality for decisions** (which prompts/sessions produce good outcomes). If routing and performance profiles get built on that data, you want it from a record that can't be quietly rewritten.
3. **Compliance answers** ("prove which agent run changed this security-critical function") need the tamper-evident version, not the brain's local notes.

So: it's really a **platform/entiredb item that the brain feeds**, not something the brain consumes — which is exactly why it's the only M-priority issue in the keystone and why it sits server-side. My recommendation stands, slightly stronger now: **defer it**, and honestly it may belong to the decentralized-architecture team rather than in a brain PR at all — same pattern as the P1 storage decision ("the brain owns the what and when; the platform owns the shared rails").

Shall I lock in the plan as: graph + brain + cli PRs in parallel, git-meta + cache, COR-785 deferred?
yes

Locked. Executing as orchestrator: worktrees first, then three parallel implementation agents building to **one frozen delta schema** (the #85/#242 wire-fork lesson — the contract gets defined once, by me, in every prompt).

**The keystone — the part between P1 and P2 — is done and shipped as three PRs**, all open for review, nothing merged:

| PR | What it delivers |
|---|---|
| [entire-graph #114](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/pull/114) | `schema_version` + `producer_version` stamped on diff output (additive, the COR-781 schema freeze) |
| [cli #2041](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2041) | `entity_deltas.json` written into each checkpoint's tree — gated **off by default**, computed by a detached child so the git hook only pays a process spawn, CAS-protected ref advance (COR-782) |
| [entire-brain #87](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/87) | The index + query: `entities backfill/history/show`, MCP tool `brain_entity_history`, contiguous-window coverage cursors, and facts now anchored to the checkpoint that actually made the change (COR-783/784) |

How it got here, in one paragraph: three builders worked in parallel against one frozen schema; two adversarial review rounds then killed the first cli and brain designs outright (a measured 3.5s hook stall and a checkpoint-orphaning ref race on the cli; a permanent index-gap poisoning and a shipped-`verify` regression on the brain) — every defect was fixed, and every fix is pinned by a mutation check (10+ across the campaign, each proven to fail its test when reverted). The live e2e ran a real repo against the real graph binary, not a fake. The doctrine killed roughly half of what the builders initially claimed, which is exactly its job.

Deferred by your call: COR-785 (transparency-log causality) — it's platform work that should follow the P1 merge.

Two housekeeping items left that only you can do: the Linear issues COR-781..784 sit **Canceled** and need reactivating to track these PRs, and the roadmap doc's keystone row can move from "Planned" to "In review." Merge order when you're ready: graph #114 first (both others' producer), then brain #87 and cli #2041 in either order.
